messages.subject: [Re: Next steps]
parts:
For information of others.

This was one of my first concerns.

Chillu (student) and I (mentor) are using a wiki page with a "diary" subpage on my virtual
server at uOttawa. We haven't yet worked out how much global access to provide to this,
but in our Automatic Differentiation project there are several folk who've offered help.
Over next week or so we'll work out the access rules, likely something with global read,
limited write access. This is nominally easy with Dokuwiki, but I've been caught once or
twice in the past.

The diary page was helpful to me in a previous (unrelated) project. A bit messy but effective.

We haven't formalized what we'll do with code, but have been talking about svn on r-forge.

JN


-------- Original Message --------
Subject: Next steps
Date: Sun, 09 May 2010 20:38:33 -0500
From: Dirk Eddelbuettel <e...@debian.org>
Reply-To: gso...@googlegroups.com
To: gsoc-r <gso...@googlegroups.com>


Hi all,

A couple of days ago, I asked how you all felt about a little structure for
the overall progress messages.

* Roger suggested r-forge, which was seconded by Felix who already set-up a
repo and project there. R-Forge is definitely a good option, its recent
struggles with uptime and power over in Vienna notwithstanding.

* Tal gave some tips for blogging and email-to-blig interfaces. Shane
seconded the choice of blogs.

* Felix then gave a nice little breakdown of possible communication lines,
from 'narrow' mentor-to-student to 'wider' community-oriented ones.

With that, led me explain better what I had in mind:

- there is definitely need for student-mentor communication, and this
mostly works in a natural way

- the R Project has been successful (or just lucky :-) in the past without
'enforcing' anything more; other project have reported success with some
'wider' communications tools -- and blogs are one easy example

- my role as admin in part encompasses playing 'backup' here, so I (as well
as the R community as a whole) want to ensure that all the pieces remain
in flow and moving.

Therefore, I would like to repeat to a suggestion to set 'something' up.
This could be a joint blogger.com or wordpress account, or even just a wiki
page (preferably with a rss/atom feed though).

These two to three months tend to fly by quickly. Many past participants have
found it helpful to keep some sort of informal timeline -- maybe weekly or
bi-monthly -- to post some status updates. More frequently works too.

So would anyone like to volunteer setting up a 'GSoC R 2010' blog account?
Or do to many of you are indifferent ? I'd love to hear from our students
here, so (in alphabetical order) Chidambaram, Colin, Felix, Ian, Yasuhisa:
how do feel about this?

That concludes the nagging message of the week :)

--
Regards, Dirk

Re: rdax project (automatic differentiation in R), Chillu has been recording a progress
diary on my optimx wiki (currently login only) and we have been in contact with Tal about
the blog backend. The diary is mainly for us, so we both can see where we are at. However,
we've been discussing what material to put on the blog and also who to alert (outside of
GSoC folk) about what is happening, as a number of workers showed interest in AD and
several offered to provide advice etc. I suspect several other projects are in a similar
situation -- some material, but not really enough to show off yet.

I also got Carol Smith's note about Welcome packages and note the matter of mid-term
evaluations. Perhaps Dirk or someone with previous experience would provide a note on the
process and timing for both mentors and students so we keep gsoc-r group in good standing.

Cheers, JN

messages.author: 7d2d2f522132a5e1
messages.subject: Re: Updates
parts:
I have been meaning to post about the progress in the ability for
automatic differentiation in R to a wider audience for quite some
time. Prof. John Nash and me already have in place, a system for
differentiation of non-singular univariate functions up to arbitrary
order, which is itself good news. However, I chose to wait to
implement a few more features before posting news about the progress
thus far. Specifically, I am currently working on multivariate
function differentiation which will conclude the development of the
forward mode of AD. My idea was that the completion of the forward
mode AD would be a logical milestone that would necessitate informing
the community at large.

However, I am sure that by the end of this week I will have a fully
functional package and a tutorial/demo that will demonstrate what can
be done using the AD engine. I am sorry for not having posted to the
blog (despite having supported the idea and saying that I would) and
keeping people in the dark about the project's progress.

The development of the package can be followed at:
http://github.com/quantumelixir/radx

Regards,
Chillu
